title: They Stole $2.7 Million in 14 Minutes — 6 Years Later, One Man Talked. Where's the Money?
description:
On January 17th, 1950, seven masked men in chauffeur's coats and Halloween masks walked into the Brink's building on Prince Street in Boston and pulled off what was then the largest robbery in American history — $2,775,395 in cash and checks, gone in fourteen minutes. No alarms. No shots fired. No trace. The FBI chased 5,000 leads and got nowhere.

Six years later, with the statute of limitations days from expiring, the case cracked — not from evidence, but from greed. Gang member Joseph 'Specs' O'Keefe felt cheated out of his cut, got shot by his own crew to silence him, survived, and started talking just eleven days before time ran out.

Eight men were convicted in 1956. But only $58,000 of the $2.7 million was ever recovered. The rest has never been found — no vault, no account, no grave has ever given it up. Subscribe now 👇
